This study examines the problem of detecting stealthy attacks on linear time-invariant systems by leveraging the system's internal model. We introduce a novel approach that utilizes a Kalman filter to generate predictions of the system's state, which are then compared against actual measurements to identify anomalies. We demonstrate that this method is capable of detecting attacks that remain undetectable by traditional residual-based techniques. Furthermore, we establish that the detection performance of this approach is equivalent to that of a Kalman filter designed for a system with a known attack model.

This study introduces GAE-ISumm, a novel unsupervised graph-based framework designed for summarizing Indian languages. The proposed method leverages a graph autoencoder to generate a low-dimensional representation of the input text, which is subsequently utilized to construct a graph where nodes represent sentences and edges denote their semantic relationships. The system identifies the most salient sentences by analyzing the graph's structural properties, specifically the degree of each node. The resulting summaries are evaluated using ROUGE metrics against human-generated references. Experimental results demonstrate that GAE-ISumm achieves superior performance compared to existing unsupervised baselines.

This paper investigates S-rings of Cohen type, which are defined as S-rings over a finite abelian group $G$ that are generated by a single element $g$ of order $|G|$. We demonstrate that such S-rings are isomorphic to the S-ring $\mathcal{S}(G, \mathcal{B})$ constructed from a specific set of subgroups $\mathcal{B}$ of $G$. Furthermore, we establish that the number of these S-rings is finite.

We have identified five nearby stars that exhibit significant acceleration, with the most extreme case being a star moving at 1.2 milliarcseconds per year. By analyzing the astrometric data from the Gaia mission, we have determined the masses and distances of the unseen companions responsible for these accelerations. Our findings indicate that the most massive companion is approximately 1.5 solar masses, while the most distant is roughly 1.5 kiloparsecs away.

Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) are a prominent class of generative models that have gained significant attention in recent years. This study introduces a novel VAE variant, the Least Squares Variational Autoencoder (LS-VAE), which employs a least squares loss function to enhance the quality of generated samples. Furthermore, we incorporate a regularization term into the model to mitigate the risk of overfitting. The proposed method is evaluated on two distinct datasets: the MNIST dataset for handwritten digit recognition and the Fashion-MNIST dataset for fashion item classification. Experimental results demonstrate that the LS-VAE outperforms the standard VAE in terms of both reconstruction accuracy and the quality of generated samples.

The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly transformed daily life, yet their widespread adoption introduces critical security and privacy challenges. This study introduces a novel IoT-based smart home gadget monitoring system that leverages private blockchain technology to ensure data integrity and security. The proposed architecture utilizes a private blockchain to store and manage data, while a localization algorithm is employed to determine the precise location of each gadget. Furthermore, the system incorporates a smart contract to facilitate the secure and efficient transfer of data between gadgets.

This study introduces a deep learning-based quantization method for L-variables in Gray-coded modulation schemes. The proposed approach employs a neural network to generate quantization levels, which are subsequently optimized using a gradient descent algorithm. The resulting quantization levels are then applied to the L-variables within the soft-input soft-output (SISO) demodulator. Simulation results demonstrate that this method achieves performance comparable to the optimal quantization levels, while offering a significant reduction in computational complexity.

We introduce a parameterized algorithm for determining the upward planarity of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) with respect to a fixed linear ordering of its vertices. The algorithm runs in $O^*(2^k)$ time, where $k$ represents the number of edges that violate the specified linear order. This result is achieved by leveraging a novel characterization of upward planarity that relies on the concept of a "canonical" linear order.

Crowdsourcing has become a standard method for gathering data, yet it frequently introduces noise and bias. This study introduces a novel approach to mitigate these issues by employing an ensemble of models trained on crowdsourced data. We evaluate the performance of this ensemble against a single model and demonstrate that it yields superior results. Furthermore, we introduce a new metric for quantifying uncertainty in crowdsourced datasets, which we term the "Human Softmax" distribution. This metric is derived from the softmax outputs of the ensemble models. We validate the effectiveness of this metric by applying it to a real-world crowdsourced dataset.

We establish a sufficient condition for the norm of the transfer operator associated with a semiflow to decrease. This result is applied to the study of the Navier-Stokes equations, specifically to demonstrate the existence of a unique invariant measure for the stochastic Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$.

This study introduces a novel construction method for strength-2 covering arrays (CAs) with small dimensions, utilizing a specific class of orthogonal arrays (OAs) and a newly defined structure called a "quasi-orthogonal array" (QOA). The proposed approach yields strength-2 CAs with fewer rows than previously known constructions for numerous parameter sets.

We demonstrate that the set of nonlocal games involving maximally correlated states is decidable, provided the states are subject to noise. This result extends the findings of [1], which established decidability for noiseless maximally correlated states.

Automated crash reproduction is a critical component of software testing, yet it remains a difficult challenge. This study presents a partial replication of a genetic algorithm designed to automatically reproduce crashes, originally proposed by the authors of the paper "A Guided Genetic Algorithm for Automated Crash Reproduction" (2019). The work evaluates the algorithm's performance on a dataset of 100 crashes from the Fuzzing Challenge 2018, comparing its results against the original authors' findings.

We report the observation of a vortex lattice transition in the high-$T_c$ cuprate superconductor $\text{Bi}_2\text{Sr}_2\text{CaCu}_2\text{O}_{8+\delta}$, which occurs at a critical magnetic field $H_{c2}^*$ and is characterized by a shift from a square to a square-square lattice structure. This transition is identified through the analysis of the magnetic field dependence of the upper critical field $H_{c2}$, the specific heat, and the temperature dependence of the upper critical field $H_{c2}$. The findings suggest that the transition is driven by the interplay between the superconducting order parameter and the magnetic field, leading to a change in the vortex lattice structure. The results are consistent with the theoretical predictions of the Ginzburg-Landau theory, which describes the behavior of the superconducting order parameter in the presence of a magnetic field. The study provides new insights into the nature of the vortex lattice transition in high-$T_c$ cuprate superconductors, and may have implications for the development of new superconducting materials with improved properties. The findings are also relevant to the understanding of the role of the vortex lattice structure in the superconducting properties of high-$T_c$ cuprate superconductors, and may have implications for the development of new superconducting materials with improved properties. We demonstrate that the anisotropic flow of thermal photons, generated during the initial stages of heavy-ion collisions, provides a direct probe of the quark-gluon plasma's shear viscosity to entropy density ratio ($\eta/s$). This capability arises because the anisotropic flow of thermal photons is highly sensitive to the initial spatial anisotropy of the system, whereas the anisotropic flow of hadrons is largely insensitive to it. Consequently, the anisotropic flow of thermal photons offers a more precise measurement of the initial spatial anisotropy, thereby enabling a more accurate determination of the quark-gluon plasma's $\eta/s$.

We introduce a comprehensive study of magnetic ordering in triangular and kagome lattices, focusing on the interplay between nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor exchange interactions. By employing a mean-field approach, we identify the ground states for various exchange parameter combinations and analyze the resulting magnetic structures. Our findings reveal that the triangular lattice supports a rich variety of magnetic orders, including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and spiral configurations. In contrast, the kagome lattice exhibits a more limited set of ground states, primarily consisting of ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and spiral orders. We further investigate the stability of these magnetic phases by examining their response to external magnetic fields.

This study introduces a novel framework for identifying treatment effects in large-scale experiments, specifically addressing scenarios where the false discovery rate (FDR) is controlled under dependence. We establish a new identification condition that accommodates both positive and negative dependence structures. Furthermore, we propose a robust procedure for estimating treatment effects that maintains FDR control under these conditions. The method's performance is validated through extensive simulations and a real-world application involving the analysis of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the stock market.

The expansion of the universe is a fundamental concept in cosmology, describing the increase in distances between galaxies over time. This phenomenon is primarily driven by the Big Bang theory, which posits that the universe originated from an extremely hot, dense state approximately 13.8 billion years ago. Since that initial event, the cosmos has been expanding, causing galaxies to move away from one another. This expansion is not merely a result of galaxies traveling through space but rather the stretching of space itself.

The rate of this expansion is quantified by the Hubble constant, which measures the speed at which galaxies recede relative to their distance from Earth. Observations indicate that this expansion is accelerating, a discovery attributed to the presence of dark energy—a mysterious force that counteracts gravity and drives the universe apart. Understanding the dynamics of cosmic expansion is crucial for determining the universe's ultimate fate, as it influences whether the cosmos will continue expanding indefinitely, collapse back in a "Big Crunch," or undergo a "Big Rip."

We investigate the type-X two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) to address the recent tensions between the muon anomalous magnetic moment and the $W$ boson mass. We demonstrate that the model can simultaneously resolve both discrepancies by introducing a light charged Higgs boson with a mass below 100 GeV.

Locating concepts within large-scale knowledge bases is a critical task for both human users and automated systems. While existing methods often rely on reformulating user queries to improve search results, they frequently fail to address the specific challenges posed by concept location. This paper introduces QUICKAR, a novel approach that leverages crowdsourced knowledge to automatically reformulate user inquiries. By utilizing a crowdsourcing platform, QUICKAR generates multiple reformulations for each query, which are then ranked using a learned model. Experimental results demonstrate that QUICKAR outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and efficiency.

Entrainment, a phenomenon where interlocutors unconsciously mimic each other's speech patterns, serves as a key indicator of social bonding and rapport. This study introduces a novel, unsupervised metric for quantifying entrainment in spoken dialogue, leveraging deep neural networks to analyze acoustic features. The proposed method is evaluated on the Entrainment Corpus, a dataset comprising 1,000 minutes of recorded conversations. Results indicate that the metric effectively captures the degree of entrainment, with a strong correlation observed between the metric's output and the actual duration of the interaction.

Temporal action segmentation (TAS) aims to identify and segment actions within video sequences. While supervised TAS methods have achieved significant success, they depend heavily on large-scale, meticulously annotated datasets. In contrast, unsupervised TAS methods offer a promising alternative by eliminating the need for such annotations. However, existing unsupervised approaches often struggle with poor performance and lack robustness. This paper introduces SSCAP, a novel unsupervised TAS framework that leverages self-supervised learning to enhance action representation. Specifically, SSCAP employs a self-supervised co-occurrence action analysis module to capture action semantics and a self-supervised action localization module to refine action boundaries. Extensive experiments on the THUMOS14 dataset demonstrate that SSCAP achieves state-of-the-art results, surpassing all current unsupervised methods.

We investigate the production and decay of the $P_c(4312)^+$ and $P_c(4440)^+$ pentaquark states, which are composed of $uudcc\bar{c}$ quarks. Utilizing the current algebra framework, we calculate the amplitudes for the reactions $J/\psi p \to P_c^+ \eta$ and $J/\psi p \to P_c^+ \pi^0$, as well as the decay $P_c^+ \to J/\psi p$. Our findings indicate that the $P_c(4312)^+$ state is predominantly generated via the $J/\psi p \to P_c^+ \eta$ channel, whereas the $P_c(4440)^+$ state is primarily produced through the $J/\psi p \to P_c^+ \pi^0$ channel. Furthermore, the decay $P_c^+ \to J/\psi p$ is found to be dominated by the $P_c(4440)^+$ state.

This study investigates the efficacy of two distinct feedback mechanisms—Inquiry-Based Conceptual Feedback (IBCF) and Traditional Thorough Feedback (TTF)—within the context of software testing education. The research aims to determine which approach more effectively enhances students' conceptual understanding of software testing. The study involved 120 undergraduate students enrolled in a software testing course at a university in the United States. Participants were randomly assigned to either the IBCF or TTF group. The findings indicate that the IBCF group demonstrated significantly higher conceptual understanding compared to the TTF group. Furthermore, the IBCF group exhibited a greater increase in conceptual understanding than the TTF group. The study concludes that the IBCF approach is more effective than the TTF approach in enhancing students' conceptual understanding of software testing.

Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) addresses the challenge of adapting a pre-trained model to a new target domain without access to the original source data. This paper introduces a novel semi-supervised SFDA framework that leverages the hypothesis shift between source and target domains. By employing a hypothesis shift estimator, the method identifies the target domain's hypothesis shift and utilizes it to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled target data. Furthermore, the approach incorporates a hypothesis shift regularizer to enhance the quality of these pseudo-labels. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

This paper examines the potential of gas core engines for deep space propulsion, focusing on the challenges of achieving high specific impulse and thrust. It reviews the current state of the art, including the NASA Gas Core Rocket (GCR) and the Nuclear Thermal Rocket (NTR), and outlines the primary obstacles to their development. The study also explores the concept of a gas core engine utilizing a liquid fuel, specifically a liquid metal, and discusses the associated challenges. Finally, the paper concludes with a summary of the key findings and recommendations for future research.

We introduce a domain-informed neural network designed to determine the interaction position of particles within astroparticle detectors. This approach leverages the physical laws governing particle propagation and energy loss, which are encoded as a neural network's loss function. We demonstrate that this method yields superior accuracy compared to standard neural networks, particularly in scenarios involving limited training data.

We introduce EXOPLINES, a comprehensive archive of molecular absorption cross-sections tailored for the atmospheres of brown dwarfs and giant exoplanets. This resource offers a unified, user-friendly interface for accessing cross-sections for 12 key molecules, including H₂O, CO, CH₄, NH₃, HCN, HNC, CS, H₂S, SO₂, H₂SO₄, H₂CO, and H₂CN. The archive is accessible via the website https://exo-planet.org/exoplins.

This paper introduces a novel approach to grounding Answer Set Programming (ASP) that is both more efficient and more flexible than existing methods. We demonstrate that this new method can be implemented using a straightforward, uniform algorithm. Furthermore, we prove that the algorithm is correct and that it is complete with respect to the standard grounding semantics.

We introduce a general framework for quantum resource theories, which encompasses the resource theories of coherence, entanglement, and asymmetry. We establish a universal initial law for these theories, demonstrating that the initial state of a quantum system is the unique state that maximizes the average resource content across all possible measurements.

We introduce a method for estimating the parameters of a probability distribution using its moments, which is particularly effective for distributions with heavy tails. This approach is applied to analyze the distribution of the number of distinct prime factors in a random integer.

This study introduces a novel Bayesian framework for analyzing heavy-tailed multivariate time series, where the tail index is treated as a random variable. We employ a hierarchical prior structure that allows the tail index to vary across time and dimensions, thereby accommodating both heavy-tailed and light-tailed behaviors. The model is implemented using a Gibbs sampler, and its performance is evaluated through simulations and an empirical analysis of the S&P 500 index.

We introduce a family of quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes that achieve a linear-time decoding complexity, specifically $O(n)$, where $n$ represents the code length. These codes are constructed by utilizing a specific class of classical LDPC codes characterized by a constant column weight and a constant row weight.

This paper introduces a distributed algorithm for constructing a distance-$r$ dominating group on graphs with high girth, where the algorithm operates in $O(r \log n)$ rounds. The algorithm is designed to function on sparse graphs, specifically those with a maximum degree of $\Delta$.

We introduce a disordered higher-order topological insulator (HOTI) in three dimensions, characterized by a bulk gap and a gapped surface, yet hosting gapless corner states. We demonstrate that the bulk-surface correspondence in this system is governed by the bulk-boundary correspondence, which is further linked to the bulk-corner correspondence. Furthermore, we establish that the bulk-surface correspondence in this disordered HOTI is equivalent to the bulk-boundary correspondence in a corresponding two-dimensional disordered topological insulator.

The CMS collaboration at the LHC has recently reported the first evidence of supersymmetry (SUSY) in the form of a light stop squark, with a mass of approximately 400 GeV. This discovery has prompted a re-evaluation of the SUSY parameter space, particularly within the context of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM). This study examines the implications of the light stop finding on the remaining SUSY spectrum, specifically focusing on the gluino and neutralino masses. We analyze the resulting parameter space using the latest CMS constraints and the most recent LHC Run 2 data.

We introduce a neural rendering framework that utilizes a single RGB image to generate a 3D representation of a scene, enabling the synthesis of novel views and the creation of 3D models. Our method employs a neural network to predict a 3D Gaussian distribution for each pixel, which is subsequently rendered into a 2D image using a differentiable renderer. This approach allows for the generation of 3D models that are compatible with standard 3D software.

The Southern Astrophysical Research (SOAR) telescope, located in Chile, is a 4.1-meter facility operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA) on behalf of its consortium. This instrument supports a wide array of scientific investigations, including high-resolution imaging, spectroscopy, and interferometry. This paper details the 2021 operational performance of the SOAR speckle interferometry system, which is designed to achieve diffraction-limited imaging at visible wavelengths. The system's capabilities are demonstrated through the analysis of 1,000 speckle images of the star $\alpha$ Orionis, which were collected over a 10-hour period.

We introduce a novel framework for the celestial chiral algebra of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, which is built upon the $SU(2)$ R-symmetry group. This construction relies on a specific $SU(2)$-covariant extension of the standard celestial chiral algebra, which we term the "celestial hue algebra." We demonstrate that this hue algebra is integrable and possesses a dual counterpart known as the "celestial kinematic algebra," which is constructed from the kinematic algebra of the standard celestial chiral algebra. We further establish that the celestial hue algebra is isomorphic to the celestial kinematic algebra, thereby establishing a "hue-kinematics duality." This duality serves as a celestial analogue to the well-known color-kinematics duality in gauge theory.

We present the first observations of a jet-driven piston blast wave in the low solar corona, captured by the LOFAR radio telescope. This event occurred on 2018 August 15, originating from a jet that erupted from a sunspot in the active region AR12673. The jet's expansion was halted by a dense coronal structure, resulting in a shock wave that propagated outward. The resulting radio emission was detected by LOFAR at 110 MHz, with the source's brightness temperature reaching approximately $10^{10}$ K. The emission spectrum exhibited a power-law distribution with a spectral index of $\alpha \approx 0.5$. Theoretical modeling indicates that the radio emission arises from the gyrosynchrotron process, driven by electrons accelerated to energies of roughly 100 keV.

We investigate the general two Higgs doublet model (2HDM) to address the flavor anomalies and the muon anomalous magnetic moment ($g-2$). By analyzing the likelihood of the flavor anomalies, we determine the preferred parameter space for the model. Subsequently, we examine the compatibility of this region with the $g-2$ measurement. Our findings indicate that the general 2HDM can simultaneously accommodate the flavor anomalies and the $g-2$ anomaly, provided the charged Higgs boson mass is approximately 1.5 TeV.

We introduce a stochastic vortex dynamics model for two-dimensional incompressible fluids, formulated as a functional stochastic differential equation (SDE) driven by a cylindrical Wiener process. This model is constructed to satisfy the Navier-Stokes equations in the mean, with the stochastic component representing the influence of unresolved small-scale turbulent fluctuations. We establish the existence and uniqueness of a solution to this SDE and demonstrate that the resulting stochastic flow is a strong solution to the Navier-Stokes equations. Furthermore, we prove that the solution to the SDE converges to the solution of the deterministic Navier-Stokes equations as the noise intensity diminishes.

We examine the entanglement within the complete state vector of boson sampling, a quantum optical process involving the interference of indistinguishable photons. We demonstrate that the entanglement entropy of the system's output state is directly proportional to the number of photons, a finding that holds true for both the full state vector and its reduced density matrix.

We introduce a novel method for learning temporal sequences from high-dimensional data, specifically designed for life science applications. This approach employs a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model the temporal dynamics of the data, with the network's hidden state serving as a representation of the current system state. To ensure the learned sequences are both short and interpretable, we apply a guided learning strategy that incorporates a loss function based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence. This function constrains the RNN's hidden state to align with a predefined target distribution. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method by applying it to a synthetic dataset and a real-world dataset derived from a yeast cell cycle experiment.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are widely recognized for their capacity to learn temporal dependencies, yet their internal mechanisms remain largely opaque. This study investigates the internal dynamics of RNNs within partially observable environments, specifically examining how they encode information about hidden states. We demonstrate that RNNs can effectively learn to represent these hidden states, and we further show that the specific encoding strategy adopted by the network is contingent upon the task at hand.

Action detection is a critical component of computer vision, yet it remains challenging due to the scarcity of labeled data. This paper introduces a novel approach to weakly-supervised action detection that leverages Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) to learn contextual information. By modeling the relationships between video frames as a graph, our method effectively captures the temporal dependencies essential for action recognition. We evaluate our approach on the UCF101 and HMDB51 datasets, demonstrating that it achieves state-of-the-art performance in weakly-supervised action detection.

The 2021 Image Similarity Challenge (ISC) was a competition designed to evaluate the performance of image similarity algorithms. This paper details the challenge's methodology, the results achieved by participating teams, and the key findings derived from the competition.

This work examines the long-term behavior of solutions to parabolic equations featuring a small parameter $\varepsilon$ that induces a degradation effect. We demonstrate that the associated diffusion process exhibits metastability, characterized by a slow transition between two distinct states. Furthermore, we establish the homogenization of the equation's solution as $\varepsilon$ approaches zero.

Federated learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a model without sharing their raw data, thereby addressing privacy concerns. However, FL faces significant challenges regarding communication costs and the risk of data leakage during model updates. To address these issues, we introduce DP-REC, a novel framework that integrates differential privacy (DP) with a randomized encoding (RE) scheme. This approach ensures that the server cannot infer any information about the clients' data, while simultaneously reducing communication overhead. We demonstrate that DP-REC achieves a superior balance between privacy and utility compared to existing methods.

We present far-ultraviolet (FUV) observations of the Taurus-Perseus-Aquila (TPA) molecular complex, utilizing the Far Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Explorer (FUSE) to examine the 900–1150 Å spectral range. Our analysis focuses on the 1100 Å emission line of C II, which serves as a tracer for the ionized carbon fraction in the interstellar medium. We find that the C II emission is spatially confined to the Taurus and Perseus regions, with no detectable signal from the Aquila complex. This absence of emission in Aquila is attributed to the presence of a dense, neutral hydrogen cloud that effectively absorbs the FUV radiation. Additionally, we observe a strong correlation between the C II emission intensity and the column density of neutral hydrogen ($N_{\rm H}$), indicating that the observed emission originates from the outer layers of the molecular clouds.

This study introduces a novel approach to table retrieval within PDF documents, utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to represent tables and their associated text. The method involves constructing a graph where nodes correspond to tables and text segments, with edges linking related elements. The GNN then generates embeddings for these nodes, which are subsequently used to retrieve tables based on query similarity. The authors evaluate this method against existing techniques, demonstrating that it achieves superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

This paper introduces a novel framework for modeling multi-stage games with incomplete information, where players possess varying levels of cognitive sophistication. We demonstrate that this approach yields a unique equilibrium, which we term the "cognitive hierarchy equilibrium." Furthermore, we establish that this equilibrium is robust to minor perturbations in the game's structure.

This study introduces a novel approach to estimating population counts in Mozambique by leveraging satellite imagery and machine learning. The methodology involves training a deep learning model to identify and count buildings, which are then used to derive population estimates. The model was trained on a dataset of 1,000 manually annotated images and subsequently evaluated on 1,000 additional images. Results indicate that the model achieves a mean average precision of 0.85 and a mean average recall of 0.82. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the resulting population estimates align closely with official census data, with a correlation coefficient of 0.92.

Approximate Membership Query (AMQ) filters are essential for efficiently managing large datasets, yet they typically incur false positives. This paper introduces a novel AMQ filter that eliminates false positives entirely. The proposed method is built upon a Bloom filter and utilizes a specific data structure called a "false positive free collection" (FPFC). The authors demonstrate that the FPFC can be implemented using a Bloom filter itself, thereby creating a recursive structure. This recursive design allows the new filter to achieve a false positive rate of zero while maintaining a space complexity that is only a constant factor larger than that of a standard Bloom filter.

We introduce a novel method for converting spinor atoms into spinor molecules by leveraging laser-induced three-body recombination. This approach is applicable to any spinor system, including those with both integer and half-integer spins. The process involves a two-step mechanism: first, a laser-driven three-body recombination event creates a spinor molecule alongside a free atom, followed by the subsequent decay of the free atom into a spinor molecule. This transformation is driven by the conservation of total spin angular momentum, which allows the system to transition from a state of $N$ spinor atoms to $N-1$ spinor molecules and one free atom. The resulting spinor molecules are characterized by a specific spin state that is determined by the initial spin configuration of the atoms. This method offers a promising route for generating spinor molecules with tailored spin states, which could be valuable for applications in quantum simulation and quantum information processing.

This study introduces a multi-resolution Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) framework designed to simulate fluid-structure interactions (FSI) involving multiple components. The method employs a multi-resolution approach to enhance computational efficiency by utilizing a coarse grid for the fluid domain and a fine grid for the solid domain. The proposed scheme is validated through two benchmark cases: a dam-break scenario and a two-phase FSI problem.

This study introduces a quantum unsupervised learning framework designed to identify patterns within unlabeled datasets. We demonstrate that this approach can be implemented on superconducting quantum processors, utilizing a variational quantum circuit to extract latent features from data. Furthermore, we present a quantum-guided learning method that leverages the insights gained from unsupervised analysis to enhance the performance of supervised learning tasks.

FastPitch is a neural network designed for text-to-speech synthesis that utilizes a pitch contour to generate speech. While it offers superior quality and controllability compared to previous models, it struggles with pitch control, particularly when the input pitch contour is noisy. This study introduces a novel method to enhance pitch controllability by employing a pitch augmentation technique that preserves timbre. This approach involves training a separate model to predict the original pitch contour from the synthesized speech, thereby enabling the generation of a new pitch contour that retains the original's timbre. Experimental results indicate that this method significantly improves pitch controllability.

We introduce Hopper, a novel transformer-based architecture designed for spatiotemporal inference. Unlike standard transformers that rely on self-attention, Hopper utilizes a hop-based attention mechanism to capture long-range dependencies. This approach allows the model to effectively learn from distant temporal and spatial contexts, thereby enhancing its ability to forecast future states. We evaluate Hopper on two distinct datasets: the UCF-Crime dataset for action recognition and the UCF-Landmarks dataset for landmark detection. Experimental results demonstrate that Hopper achieves state-of-the-art performance on both tasks.

This study presents a measurement of the $W$ boson mass utilizing the $W \to \ell\nu$ decay channel, where $\ell$ represents either an electron or a muon, in conjunction with a $b\bar{b}$ pair. The analysis utilizes the full dataset collected by the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $138\text{ fb}^{-1}$ at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 13\text{ TeV}$. The $W$ boson mass is extracted by fitting the transverse mass distribution of the $W$ boson, which is reconstructed from the lepton and missing transverse momentum. The resulting value is $m_W = 80.434 \pm 0.036\text{ (stat)} \pm 0.044\text{ (syst)}\text{ GeV}$.

This study introduces a novel framework for evaluating the quality of experience (QoE) in telepresence robots, specifically focusing on the impact of latency and bandwidth on user satisfaction. We conducted a user study involving 10 participants who controlled a robot to navigate a virtual environment, with the system's performance metrics recorded. Our analysis reveals that QoE is significantly influenced by both latency and bandwidth, with latency exerting a more pronounced effect. Furthermore, we identified a critical threshold for latency beyond which QoE deteriorates sharply.

This paper introduces Bayesian hierarchical linear models (HLMs) as a flexible framework for analyzing data with nested structures, such as students within classrooms or patients within hospitals. It outlines the model's components, including priors, likelihoods, and hyperpriors, and demonstrates how to specify and fit these models using the R programming language.

The Mafia game is a social deduction activity where players are secretly assigned roles as either Mafia or civilians, with the Mafia aiming to eliminate all civilians while civilians strive to identify and remove the Mafia. This paper introduces a mathematical model of the game, analyzing the probability of the Mafia's victory under various conditions. We demonstrate that the Mafia's win rate is contingent upon the number of Mafia members, the total number of players, and the specific elimination rules employed. Furthermore, we derive a formula for the Mafia's win probability and validate it through computer simulations.

We investigate the concurrent gas accretion of two giant planets within a protoplanetary disk, focusing on the influence of their orbital separation on the final mass of the planets and the disk's structural evolution. Our findings indicate that the final mass of the planets is primarily determined by the initial mass of the disk and the orbital separation between the planets. Furthermore, the disk's structure is significantly altered by the presence of the planets, with the degree of modification depending on the orbital separation.

We report the first experimental observation of phonon-assisted intertube electronic conduction in a film of armchair carbon nanotubes. This phenomenon is identified through a distinct peak in the temperature-dependent resistance, which occurs at a specific temperature ($T_{peak}$) that scales with the square root of the applied bias voltage ($V$). This behavior is consistent with a theoretical model describing phonon-assisted tunneling between nanotubes.

Fuzzy k-means clustering is a popular unsupervised learning technique that assigns data points to clusters based on their degree of membership. However, its performance degrades in high-dimensional spaces due to the "curse of dimensionality," which causes the distance metric to become less meaningful. To address this, we introduce a novel algorithm that integrates entropy-driven feature weighting with fuzzy k-means. This approach dynamically adjusts feature weights based on their information content, effectively mitigating the impact of irrelevant dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms standard fuzzy k-means and other existing techniques in terms of clustering accuracy and stability when applied to high-dimensional datasets.

Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have recently achieved significant success in large-scale deep learning, yet their training remains challenging due to the difficulty of learning the gating network. This paper introduces a novel, consistent, and efficient algorithm for training MoE models. We demonstrate that our approach achieves a convergence rate of $O(1/T)$, which is optimal for non-convex problems. Furthermore, we establish that the algorithm is consistent, meaning it converges to a global optimum.

We introduce a novel class of chip-firing games on graphs, termed "Prym games," which are defined by a specific subset of vertices. We demonstrate that the Jacobian of the associated graph decomposes into a direct sum of Jacobians of smaller graphs, each corresponding to a Prym game. Furthermore, we establish that the Jacobian of a graph is isomorphic to the Prym Jacobian of a specific graph derived from it.

We examine the possibility of detecting global symmetry breaking in quantum gravity through the observation of cosmic double refraction. This phenomenon would manifest as a rotation of the polarization plane of light from distant sources, a rotation that is proportional to the light's wavelength and the distance traveled. We demonstrate that the current observational limits on this effect impose stringent constraints on the energy scale at which global symmetries break down.

We present a UVIT investigation of the globular cluster NGC 4147, utilizing data from the 2018 observing run. The study focuses on the cluster's UV bright stars, which are identified as the most luminous members of the cluster. We have determined the cluster's distance modulus to be $(m-M)_0 = 18.85 \pm 0.05$ mag, a value consistent with prior literature. Additionally, we have derived the cluster's age and metallicity as $11.5 \pm 0.5$ Gyr and $[Fe/H] = -1.1 \pm 0.1$ dex, respectively.

The Mumford conjecture, proven by Lannes and Zarati, asserts that the stable cohomology of the moduli space of curves is a polynomial algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$ generated by classes of degree $2p^k-2$ for $k \geq 2$. This paper establishes a new proof of the conjecture by demonstrating that the moduli space of curves satisfies the $b$-principle.

The transferability of deep learning models is a critical factor in their practical application. This study investigates the transferability of pre-trained models across various tasks, specifically examining the impact of the number of training samples and the degree of domain shift. Our findings indicate that the transferability of pre-trained models is not absolute; rather, it is contingent upon the specific task and the quantity of available training data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the transferability of pre-trained models is not uniform across all layers, with the degree of transferability varying significantly depending on the layer's position within the network.

This study investigates how network modularity influences the velocity of information spread. We demonstrate that modularity acts as a critical factor in determining diffusion speed, with the rate of information propagation being inversely proportional to the modularity of the network. Furthermore, we establish that the speed of diffusion is directly linked to the modularity of the network's complement.
We establish a quantitative version of the Thomas-Yau conjecture, demonstrating that the distinctiveness of a Calabi-Yau metric is bounded below by the volume of its moduli space.

This study introduces a discrete-time precision analysis for the time-domain regular perturbation model applied to unamplified links. The analysis demonstrates that the model's precision is contingent upon the number of perturbation terms included, the link's length, and the specific dispersion characteristics. Furthermore, the study derives a closed-form expression for the model's precision, which is subsequently validated through numerical simulations.

Android serves as the most prevalent mobile operating system, yet it remains vulnerable to various security threats. This paper examines the Android issue space, specifically focusing on evasion attacks that bypass security mechanisms. We categorize these attacks into two primary types: those targeting the kernel and those targeting the user space. The kernel-level evasion attacks are further divided into two subcategories: those that exploit kernel vulnerabilities and those that utilize kernel features. Conversely, user-space evasion attacks are classified into two subcategories: those that exploit user-space vulnerabilities and those that leverage user-space features. We also provide a comprehensive survey of existing evasion attacks, detailing their methodologies and the specific security mechanisms they bypass.

This paper introduces Ozy, a container orchestration system designed to manage the lifecycle of containers across a cluster. Ozy is built upon a novel architecture that separates the control plane from the data plane, enabling the system to handle a vast number of containers with minimal overhead. The system's design prioritizes scalability, fault tolerance, and high availability.

We report the observation of a reentrant 5/2 quantum Hall state in a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure, which exhibits a pronounced dependence on Landau-level mixing. This state is characterized by a distinct peak in longitudinal resistance, $R_{xx}$, occurring at a specific filling factor $\nu = 5/2$. The peak's position shifts with magnetic field strength, and its magnitude is modulated by the sample's electron density.

We demonstrate that the Thakurta metric, which describes a black hole with a cosmological constant, is not a valid solution to the Einstein field equations. Consequently, the Thakurta metric cannot be used to model cosmological black holes. This finding does not alter the existing constraints on primordial black holes derived from LIGO-Virgo observations.

We investigate the impact of density fluctuations on the formation of planetary cores via pebble accretion, utilizing a 2D hydrodynamic simulation of a protoplanetary disk. Our results indicate that the growth rate of a planetary core is significantly influenced by the amplitude of these fluctuations. Specifically, the core's growth rate increases with the amplitude of the density fluctuations.

We demonstrate that the overparameterization of neural networks is a natural outcome of computational constraints. Specifically, we prove that for any function class, the minimum number of parameters required to approximate it within a given error bound is equivalent to the minimum number of parameters needed to approximate it within a slightly larger error bound. This equivalence holds under the assumption that the approximation is performed by a neural network with a fixed architecture.

This paper extends the results of [1] to the context of enumerable abelian groups. We establish that for any finite set $A$ within an enumerable abelian group $G$, the Bohr set $B(A)$ is contained in the sumset $A+A$ whenever the Bohr radius $\rho$ satisfies $\rho \geq 1/|A|$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Bohr set $B(A)$ is a subset of the sumset $A+A+A$ provided the Bohr radius $\rho$ is at least $1/|A|^2$.

This study introduces a branch-and-cut algorithm designed to solve the Urban Dial-a-Ride Problem (UDARP), a variant of the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) that incorporates pickup and delivery constraints. The UDARP is particularly relevant for urban environments where vehicles must transport passengers between specific locations within strict time limits. The proposed method employs a branch-and-cut framework utilizing a specialized set of valid inequalities to enhance solution efficiency. Computational experiments demonstrate that the algorithm successfully solves instances with up to 100 customers to optimality within a 1-hour time limit.

We introduce a multi-modal pretraining framework designed for e-commerce, which integrates both visual and textual data. Our approach employs a knowledge-understanding pretraining strategy that leverages a knowledge graph to enhance the model's ability to comprehend the relationships between entities. This method is applied to a multi-modal e-commerce retrieval task, where the model learns to match images with their corresponding textual descriptions. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that causes memory loss and cognitive decline, ultimately leading to death. Early diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment, yet current methods often rely on expensive and invasive procedures. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to predict the progression of AD using only non-invasive, low-cost data. The proposed method employs a deep InfoMax network to extract features from longitudinal data, which are then fed into a classifier to forecast disease progression. The model was evaluated on the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches.

This study introduces a novel approach to language semantics comprehension utilizing an interaction-based recurrent neural network. The model employs a bidirectional LSTM to capture the sequential dependencies inherent in natural language, while a self-attention mechanism is integrated to facilitate the interaction between words and their surrounding context. The proposed architecture is evaluated on the Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST) dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a model for a correlated metal featuring spin-orbit coupling, where the coupling strength is modulated by the local spin state. This framework captures the essential physics of the recently discovered material, $\text{CePt}_3\text{Si}$. We demonstrate that the interplay between spin-orbit coupling and the Kondo effect generates a novel form of spin-orbit coupling, termed "augmented spin-orbit coupling." This phenomenon is characterized by a significantly enhanced coupling constant and a distinct dependence on the Fermi energy.

We introduce a novel class of matter, termed "conformal shadow matter," which is characterized by a conformal equation of state and a negative squared sound speed. This matter is hypothesized to exist in a metastable state, potentially accounting for the observed dark energy density. We demonstrate that this model can be constructed within a framework of scalar-tensor gravity, specifically utilizing a scalar field with a non-minimal coupling to gravity.

The efficacy of AI-driven medical devices is frequently evaluated using test sets that differ from the training data distribution. This study introduces a novel framework for estimating the efficacy of such devices under distribution shifts by leveraging conformal prediction. We demonstrate that this approach offers a more reliable assessment of efficacy compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the framework's performance and validate its effectiveness through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

We introduce a novel molecular dynamics approach for DNA that utilizes a rigid substrate to bias the system toward specific conformations. This method is designed to facilitate the sampling of rare events, such as the transition between B- and A-form DNA. By employing a rigid substrate, the approach effectively reduces the dimensionality of the conformational space, thereby accelerating the sampling of these rare events. The method is validated by demonstrating the transition from B- to A-form DNA, which is achieved by applying a biasing potential to the system.

The ANS (Arithmetic Number System) is a highly efficient entropy encoding method that has been widely adopted in various compression algorithms. This study evaluates the ANS's performance across a range of compression scenarios, including the compression of raw data, the compression of data already compressed by other methods, and the compression of data that has undergone lossy compression. The results indicate that the ANS is a highly effective entropy encoder, capable of achieving compression ratios that are comparable to or even surpass those of the arithmetic coding method.

The dielectric properties of pore solutions within cement-based materials are examined through the lens of the Debye model, which describes the relaxation of dipole moments. This study investigates how the dielectric constant and relaxation time vary with temperature and the concentration of dissolved ions. The findings indicate that the dielectric constant increases with temperature, whereas the relaxation time decreases. Furthermore, the relaxation time is observed to be inversely proportional to the concentration of dissolved ions.

This paper reviews the current status of hadronic molecular states composed of heavy mesons and baryons, with a specific focus on those involving at least one heavy quark. We examine the theoretical frameworks used to describe these systems, including the non-relativistic quark model, the Bethe-Salpeter equation, and the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model. Additionally, we discuss the experimental evidence for these states and their potential applications in the study of the quark-gluon plasma.

This study examines the drivers behind the development of military swarm unmanned systems. By utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, the research analyzes a corpus of 1,000 documents sourced from the German Federal Ministry of Defence (BMVg) and the German Aerospace Center (DLR). The analysis identifies key drivers, including the need for increased operational efficiency, the necessity for greater operational flexibility, and the requirement for enhanced operational resilience.

We introduce a novel method for extracting cosmological parameters directly from the three-dimensional Lyman-$\alpha$ forest, utilizing the full covariance matrix of the power spectrum. This approach is designed to be robust against systematic errors and is applicable to both current and future large-scale surveys. We demonstrate the method's efficacy by applying it to the SDSS-III BOSS DR11 dataset, successfully recovering the matter power spectrum and the Hubble parameter. Furthermore, we show that the technique can effectively constrain the matter density parameter ($\Omega_m$) and the amplitude of matter fluctuations ($\sigma_8$) when combined with external data from the cosmic microwave background.

We report the first observation of transverse and longitudinal emittance transfer in a storage ring, achieved by utilizing a novel technique that employs a dedicated kicker magnet to induce a controlled transverse kick. This method allows for the precise measurement of the transfer function, which is subsequently used to determine the emittance transfer coefficient.

This study introduces a novel trajectory prediction framework that integrates a sliding window approach with a Socially-Aware CVAE. The model leverages a sliding window to capture the temporal dynamics of the target vehicle's trajectory, while the Socially-Aware CVAE component models the interactions between the target and surrounding agents. To enhance prediction accuracy, the framework incorporates a reevaluation mechanism that dynamically adjusts the sliding window size based on the target's current state. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

Boltzmann machines are a class of stochastic neural networks that have been extensively studied for their capacity to model complex probability distributions. This study evaluates the performance of three distinct information-theoretic metrics—Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Jensen-Shannon, and Wasserstein distances—in quantifying the complexity of these distributions. We demonstrate that the Wasserstein distance is the most effective metric for this purpose, as it exhibits a strong correlation with the number of parameters in the Boltzmann machine.

This study introduces a novel approach to human-swarm interaction, enabling a human operator to control a swarm of robots using hand gestures. The system leverages a deep learning model to identify these gestures, which are then translated into specific commands for the robots. The proposed method is designed to be decentralized, allowing the human to guide the swarm without needing to know the precise location of each individual robot. The system's performance was evaluated through both simulation and real-world experiments, demonstrating its ability to accurately recognize gestures and successfully execute corresponding commands.

This study introduces a novel approach to classifying blood cells by merging two distinct neural network architectures: a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a recurrent neural network (RNN). The CNN is tasked with extracting features from the input images, while the RNN processes these features to generate the final classification. The proposed method was evaluated on the public dataset from the 2018 International Blood Cell Image Analysis Challenge (ICBIA 2018). Results indicate that the combined model outperformed both individual architectures, achieving a 99.1% accuracy rate.

We introduce a variational counterdiabatic (CD) protocol designed to initialize the ground state of the Hubbard model. This method employs a variational ansatz to approximate the CD driving term, which is then optimized using the time-dependent variational principle. We demonstrate that this approach successfully prepares the ground state of the Hubbard model across a range of parameters, including those where the system undergoes a phase transition.

This study introduces a novel empirical method for tone mapping that leverages the relationship between color temperature and luminance. The approach is designed to be computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications. The proposed method is evaluated against established techniques, including Reinhard's, Drago's, and Durand's algorithms, demonstrating superior performance in both visual quality and computational speed.
This paper introduces a novel Taylor expansion for the exponential function, which is derived from the standard Taylor series of the sine function.

We establish that any harmonic branched covering of a sphere with curvature bounded below by $m$ is a homeomorphism, provided the degree of the map is sufficiently small. This result extends the classical uniformization theorem for spheres to the setting of CAT($m$) spaces.

We introduce a laser-plasma framework designed to investigate photon-photon interactions, specifically focusing on the generation of high-energy photons via the nonlinear Compton scattering of laser photons by relativistic electrons. This process is followed by the inverse Compton scattering of these high-energy photons against a second laser pulse. We demonstrate that this method can produce high-energy photons with energies reaching up to 100 GeV.

We examine the sensitivity of the LHC to the soft-breaking $Z_2$ parameter $m_{12}$ within the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (2HDM), specifically analyzing the $m_{12}$-dependent decay rates of the heavy Higgs bosons $H$ and $A$ into pairs of lighter Higgs bosons ($H$ and $A$). We demonstrate that the LHC can probe the $m_{12}$ parameter up to approximately 100 GeV, contingent upon the masses of the heavy Higgs bosons $H$ and $A$ being sufficiently large.

This paper introduces a method for converting relational data into RDF, specifically designed to handle shape expression schemas. The approach is grounded in a formal framework that defines the semantics of shape expressions and their corresponding RDF representations. The study also examines the impact of shape expressions on the resulting RDF data, particularly regarding the preservation of data semantics.

This paper introduces pyStoNED, a Python-based toolkit designed for convex regression and frontier estimation. The software is built upon the CVXPY library and offers a user-friendly interface for implementing convex regression models. It supports various estimation methods, including the NED, NED-2, and NED-3 approaches, as well as the NED-2 and NED-3 variants. The toolkit also provides functions for calculating efficiency scores and generating visualizations. The authors demonstrate the utility of pyStoNED by applying it to a dataset of 1,000 firms from the S&P 500 index, estimating their production frontiers using the NED-2 and NED-3 methods. The results indicate that the NED-2 method yields higher efficiency scores than the NED-3 method, suggesting that the NED-2 method is more appropriate for this dataset. The authors conclude that pyStoNED is a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners interested in convex regression and frontier estimation.

We present a search for a heavy Higgs boson ($\phi$) within the $t\bar{t}\phi$ production channel at the LHC, utilizing the full Run 2 dataset from the ATLAS experiment, which corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$ at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The analysis targets the decay mode $\phi \to \tau^+\tau^-$, where the $\tau$ leptons are identified as hadronic jets. The study examines the invariant mass spectrum of the $\tau^+\tau^-$ system, searching for resonant structures indicative of a heavy Higgs boson. No significant excess above the Standard Model background is observed. Consequently, we establish exclusion limits at 95% confidence level for the production cross-section times branching ratio ($\sigma \times \text{BR}$) of the $t\bar{t}\phi$ process. These limits are derived for a range of Higgs masses between 150 and 1000 GeV, assuming a coupling strength of $g_{t\bar{t}\phi} = 1$ and a branching ratio of $\text{BR}(\phi \to \tau^+\tau^-) = 1$.

We introduce a novel approach to analyzing pretrained language models (PLMs) that leverages their inherent knowledge to perform unsupervised and few-shot tasks. Our method involves training a lightweight classifier on top of a PLM's hidden states, which is then used to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled data. These pseudo-labels facilitate the creation of a new dataset, which is subsequently employed to train a second classifier. This iterative process continues until the model converges. We demonstrate that this approach is effective for both unsupervised and few-shot scenarios, achieving performance that rivals or exceeds that of state-of-the-art supervised models.

This paper introduces a new open-source speech recognition system for German, developed using the Kaldi framework. The system is trained on the German Common Voice dataset, which contains over 100,000 hours of audio. The authors report that the system achieves a word error rate of 10.2% on the German Common Voice test set. The system is available at https://github.com/german-common-voice/german-common-voice.

We present a study of the Be star population within the 30 Doradus region, utilizing optical photometry and spectroscopy from the VLT/FLAMES survey. Our analysis reveals that the majority of these stars are located in the upper main sequence, with a few exhibiting characteristics of evolved stars. The observed Be stars display a wide range of spectral types, spanning from B0 to B9.5, and their circumstellar disks exhibit diverse properties, including varying sizes, velocities, and mass loss rates.

Text normalization is a critical component of Natural Language Processing, specifically for converting written text into its spoken form. This study introduces a novel data augmentation technique designed to enhance the performance of data-driven inverse text normalization (ITN) models. By leveraging the inherent ambiguity of ITN, the proposed method generates multiple valid ITN outputs for a single input, thereby expanding the training dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that this augmentation strategy significantly boosts the performance of ITN models.
This study establishes the Faber-Krahn inequality for the Hermite operator subject to Robin boundary conditions.

We introduce a novel kernel function, termed the Non-Exchangeable Tangent Kernel (NFT-K), designed to capture the geometric structure of data residing on manifolds. This kernel is constructed by integrating a tangent kernel with a non-exchangeable kernel, thereby combining the benefits of both. We demonstrate that the NFT-K is positive definite and possesses a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) that is isometrically equivalent to the tensor product of the RKHSs of its constituent kernels. Furthermore, we establish that the NFT-K is universal on compact manifolds. Finally, we present a theoretical analysis of the convergence rate for the NFT-K-based regularized least squares estimator.

We investigate the topological properties of one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems, specifically focusing on the point-gap topology. We demonstrate that the point-gap topology of a non-Hermitian system can be reduced by introducing correlations between its constituent subsystems. This reduction is achieved by analyzing the point-gap topology of the system's reduced density matrix. We further show that the point-gap topology of the reduced density matrix is determined by the point-gap topology of the original system and the point-gap topology of the subsystems.

We propose a new architecture that integrates a speaker encoder with a speaker encoder, which is trained to extract speaker-specific features from speech. We propose a model featuring a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry and a discrete $A_4$ symmetry, which serves as a viable framework for light dark matter. In this setup, the $A_4$ symmetry is responsible for generating the observed neutrino mass spectrum and mixing patterns, while the $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry ensures the stability of the dark matter candidate.

This study investigates the collective dynamics of triaxial nuclei by employing the minimal length concept within the framework of the Bohr-Mottelson model. We derive the corresponding Hamiltonian and solve the Schrödinger equation to obtain the energy spectrum and wave functions. The resulting energy levels are compared with experimental data for the triaxial nucleus $^{152}\text{Sm}$, demonstrating that the minimal length concept yields a more accurate description of the energy spectrum than the standard Bohr-Mottelson model.

This paper introduces a novel design for polyphase Golay complementary arrays (PGCA) by utilizing the properties of Golay complementary sequences (GCS) and Golay complementary arrays (GCA). The proposed PGCA design is derived from a GCA constructed using GCS, and the resulting PGCA exhibits a complementary array property. The paper also provides a proof demonstrating that the proposed PGCA design is optimal.

This study introduces a novel unsupervised change detection framework for hyperspectral imagery, leveraging deep convolutional neuromodulators (DCNMs) to extract features from both pre- and post-event images. The proposed architecture employs a feature fusion strategy that integrates the outputs of two separate DCNMs, which are trained independently on the respective images. This fusion mechanism is designed to capture both shared and distinct features between the two datasets. The resulting fused feature maps are then processed by a fully connected layer to generate the final change detection output. The efficacy of this approach is validated through experiments on two distinct hyperspectral datasets, demonstrating that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study investigates the link between residual entropy and viscosity in molecular fluids and model potentials. We demonstrate that the residual entropy of a fluid can be expressed as a function of the ratio between the fluid's viscosity and the viscosity of a hard-sphere fluid. This relationship holds true for both Lennard-Jones and Weeks-Chandler-Anderson fluids, as well as for the Lennard-Jones fluid with a cutoff radius of 2.5σ.

We introduce a cyclic cosmological model that incorporates the $\Lambda$CDM framework, featuring a scalar field that transitions from a negative to a positive potential. This transition facilitates a smooth shift from a contracting phase to an expanding one, thereby resolving the Big Bang singularity. The model's predictions align with current observational data, including the cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, and supernovae.

This study examines the Invariant-set theory, a superdeterministic hidden-variable framework, by analyzing its implications for Bell's theorem. We demonstrate that the theory's predictions align with quantum mechanics, thereby resolving the conflict between quantum mechanics and local realism.

Keyphrase spotting is a critical task for information retrieval, yet it remains underutilized in IoT applications due to the high computational costs of traditional methods. This study introduces a lightweight neural network designed for keyphrase spotting, which is optimized for deployment on IoT devices. The proposed architecture employs a hybrid approach, combining a convolutional neural network with a recurrent neural network. Experimental results demonstrate that this model achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods while requiring significantly fewer computational resources.

We examine the critical behavior of the dimer model on a two-dimensional lattice in the presence of a background gauge field. This study demonstrates that the dimer model is equivalent to a system of free fermions, which can be analyzed using the fermionic path integral formalism. We derive the fermionic action and establish the correspondence between the dimer model's partition function and the fermionic partition function. Furthermore, we calculate the fermionic partition function and the associated free energy, showing that the free energy is proportional to the logarithm of the dimer model's partition function. Finally, we compute the fermionic free energy and the dimer model's free energy, demonstrating that the dimer model's free energy is proportional to the logarithm of the fermionic free energy.

We introduce a novel penalized likelihood approach for high-dimensional categorical data, designed to enhance the Group Lasso method. This method employs a penalty term that incorporates the log-likelihood of the data, thereby improving the estimation of group effects. We demonstrate that this approach yields superior performance compared to the standard Group Lasso, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional data.

This paper introduces T-Visor, a hypervisor designed for mixed-criticality embedded real-time systems that leverages hardware virtualization. The system is built upon the Xen hypervisor, which is modified to support the specific requirements of embedded environments. T-Visor enables the coexistence of multiple virtual machines (VMs) with varying criticality levels on a single physical platform. It achieves this by utilizing the Xen hypervisor to isolate VMs and the Linux kernel to manage the host system. The architecture ensures that high-criticality VMs are isolated from the host and low-criticality VMs, thereby preventing interference between them. Furthermore, the system guarantees that high-criticality VMs meet their real-time deadlines even when the host or low-criticality VMs experience failures.

This study introduces a novel method for panoramic image stitching that leverages gravity priors to enhance the accuracy of feature matching. By utilizing gravity information, the approach effectively mitigates the impact of outliers and significantly improves the precision of the resulting panorama.

We investigate the synchronization dynamics of two identical populations of phase oscillators, where each oscillator exhibits a random natural frequency drawn from a uniform distribution. The study examines how the system's behavior changes as the coupling strength varies, specifically analyzing the transition from a chimera state to a fully synchronized state.

This paper introduces a model-based reinforcement learning framework designed to learn robust regulators for linear systems subject to bounded disturbances. The proposed method employs a probabilistic model of the system dynamics to guide the search for a robust regulator. The resulting algorithm is proven to converge to a robust regulator that minimizes the worst-case cost. Furthermore, the study provides a theoretical analysis of the algorithm's sample complexity.

We introduce a new class of algebras, termed higher slice algebras, which are defined as the algebras of endomorphisms of the higher slice spectrum. We demonstrate that these algebras are equivalent to the algebras of endomorphisms of the multi-layer diagram spectrum. Furthermore, we establish that the multi-layer diagram spectrum is the initial object within the category of multi-layer diagram spectra.

We investigate the information-theoretic properties of random tensor networks, specifically examining the mutual information between a boundary region and its complement. Our findings indicate that this mutual information is governed by the boundary area, with a correction term that scales as the square root of the boundary area.

We introduce a stochastic model of a one-dimensional lattice where particles move randomly and interact with their neighbors. This system is designed to study how information persists over time. We demonstrate that the system's long-term behavior is governed by a specific pattern of particle density, which is determined by the initial conditions. This pattern is robust against perturbations and can be used to store information. We also show that the system can be used to perform simple computations, such as adding two numbers. Our results suggest that this type of system could be used to create a new type of computer that is more efficient than traditional computers.

This study examines the three-dimensional generalized Hénon model, a system of three coupled nonlinear difference equations. We analyze the system's dynamics by identifying its fixed points and determining their stability, alongside the computation of Lyapunov exponents. Furthermore, we generate visualizations of the system's attractors using the Poincaré section method.
We demonstrate that the gravitational holonomy of a spacetime is uniquely determined by the spacetime's metric.

We establish a formula for the count of partitions of $n$ where every hook length is divisible by 2 or 3, and we derive a corresponding formula for partitions where every hook length is divisible by 3.

We introduce a Larmor clock approach to measure the tunneling duration of a spin-1/2 particle traversing a potential barrier. By analyzing the spin's precession, we demonstrate that the tunneling time is governed by the spin's fluctuations.
We present the leading-twist distribution functions for P-wave nonrelativistic mesons, which are derived from the light-cone expansion of the corresponding meson's light-cone wave function.

We demonstrate that the BMS geometry of asymptotically flat spacetimes is equivalent to the geometry of a null hypersurface in a specific spacetime. This equivalence allows us to derive the double soft theorem for gravitons from the BMS Ward identity. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the BMS charges and the charges of the dual null hypersurface, which facilitates the derivation of the double soft theorem for gravitons from the BMS Ward identity.

Continual learning (CL) aims to enable machines to acquire new knowledge from sequential data streams without forgetting previously learned information. While existing CL methods have been extensively studied, they often struggle with the "catastrophic forgetting" problem, where new data overwrites old knowledge. This paper introduces a novel neural architecture designed for online ensemble continual learning, which effectively mitigates forgetting by integrating multiple neural networks. The proposed approach employs a dynamic ensemble strategy that automatically adjusts the contribution of each network based on the specific task at hand. Furthermore, the system utilizes a specialized gating mechanism to regulate the flow of information between networks, ensuring that knowledge is retained and utilized appropriately. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in both accuracy and stability.

This paper investigates the permutation properties of the function $f(x) = x^{q^2+q+1} + \alpha x^{q^2+q} + \beta x^q + \gamma x$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^3}$, where $q$ is a prime power and $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in \mathbb{F}_{q^3}$. We establish that $f$ is a permutation polynomial on $\mathbb{F}_{q^3}$ if and only if $\alpha = 0$ and $\beta \neq 0$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that $f$ constitutes a total permutation polynomial on $\mathbb{F}_{q^3}$ if and only if $\alpha = 0$, $\beta \neq 0$, and $\gamma = 0$.

This study introduces a novel approach for categorizing intestinal parasites using deep belief networks (DBNs). The methodology involves training a DBN on a dataset of 1,000 images, each depicting a single parasite species, to classify them into 10 distinct categories. The results demonstrate that the DBN achieves a classification accuracy of 99.9%, surpassing the performance of a standard convolutional neural network (CNN) by 1.1%.

This study examines a non-zero-sum game involving two competing agents, each managing a portfolio of assets and a reserve fund. The agents' strategies involve investing in a risky asset and purchasing reinsurance to mitigate liability claims. The underlying asset dynamics are modeled using a regime-switching jump-diffusion process. The primary objective is to determine the Nash equilibrium for this game. To achieve this, we employ a numerical approach based on the finite difference method, utilizing a Markov chain to approximate the regime-switching component. The resulting numerical scheme is proven to be convergent, and the findings are illustrated through numerical examples.

This study introduces a novel approach to the dual simplex algorithm, which is designed to solve linear programming problems. The method incorporates a probabilistic element to enhance the algorithm's stability and smoothness. The proposed algorithm is evaluated against the standard dual simplex algorithm, demonstrating superior performance in terms of stability and smoothness. The algorithm is then applied to the problem of flight control, where it is used to generate smooth and stable flight trajectories. The results indicate that the proposed algorithm is capable of generating smooth and stable flight trajectories, which are superior to those generated by the standard dual simplex algorithm.

We examine the low-energy pion-nucleon interaction, focusing on the role of the $\pi N$ scattering length and the $\pi N$ sigma term. We demonstrate that the $\pi N$ scattering length is a fundamental quantity, whereas the $\pi N$ sigma term is not.

The CMS Phase-1 Pixel Pilot Blade, a prototype for the Phase-1 upgrade, is designed to enhance the detector's performance by increasing the number of readout channels and improving the granularity of the pixel sensors. This study examines the reconstruction of the Phase-1 Pixel Pilot Blade using the CMS Phase-1 Pixel Software Framework. The analysis focuses on the reconstruction of tracks and vertices, as well as the evaluation of the system's performance in terms of efficiency and resolution.

We present a machine learning approach to classify the morphologies of active galactic nucleus (AGN) host galaxies at redshifts $z < 1$ using the Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) Wide Survey. Our method employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on the HSC $g$-band images of 1,000 AGN hosts, with labels derived from the Galaxy Zoo 2 project. The CNN achieves a classification accuracy of 80% for the HSC sample, surpassing the 60% accuracy of a random forest classifier. We further validate the CNN's performance by applying it to a separate test set of 1,000 AGN hosts from the HSC $g$-band survey, which were not included in the training phase. This external validation yields a classification accuracy of 78%, confirming the model's robustness.

This study introduces a phase-space representation of SRCs, defined by the relative momentum and the pair's total momentum. We demonstrate that the probability of finding a nucleon pair within a specific phase-space volume is proportional to the product of the pair's momentum distribution and the pair's momentum distribution.
